merger_description:
Tetra Tech Australia Group Holdings Pty Ltd (**Tetra Tech**) proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Pitt & Sherry (Operations) Pty Ltd and its subsidiaries (**Pitt & Sherry**) through a Share Sale and Purchase Agreement (the **Acquisiti****on**).

Tetra Tech is a wholly owned subsidiary of Tetra Tech, Inc., a global public corporation listed on the NASDAQ, and the holding company for various subsidiaries. It is headquartered in Pasadena, California. Tetra Tech’s subsidiaries are involved in a variety of industries, in particular, water, energy, infrastructure, mining and resources, defence and development, and provide high-end consulting, technical and advisory services in Australia to a variety of customers, both public and private. Tetra Tech also has operations and interests across the Asia-Pacific region.

Pitt & Sherry is an Australian-based consultancy firm offering engineering, environmental and building surveying services Australia-wide, with a strong presence in Tasmania.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of engineering
consulting services to customers is low, both on a national
and state basis
b. there are alternative suppliers of engineering consulting
services to customers across Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
